candidates.title: The perfect five stars sells less: a visible flaw is what makes a brand believable (Dove r/eal reviews 2026 + Spiegel ratings research + pratfall effect 1966 + Oct 2026 FTC fake-review actions)
candidates.class: evergreen (with emerging campaign evidence + breaking enforcement spark)

sources.claim: Dove 'r/eal Reviews': invited Redditors to try the Intensive Repair 10-in-1 Serum Hair Mask and published the first 50 reviews unedited, with permission, including negative ones (e.g. 'it kinda smells like expired hotel shampoo', which 'still made the campaign'), on NYC out-of-home, social and a Manhattan pop-up. Reported: over 1 billion impressions, hour-long pop-up queues, 150+ UGC pieces; mask sales up (no figure). Emily Barfoot: 'Transparency wasn't a risk. It was our strategy.'

sources.publisher: Medill Spiegel Research Center, Northwestern University
sources.claim: Purchase likelihood typically peaks at average ratings of 4.0-4.7 and declines as ratings approach 5.0 ('too good to be true'). A product with five reviews is 270% more likely to be bought than one with none. Sample size not stated on the page.

48 male students heard a taped quiz candidate, high or average ability, with or without spilling coffee. The blunder raised liking for the highly capable candidate and lowered it for the average one; the blunder alone had no significant effect. A flaw only helps when competence is already clear.

H1 2026 best campaigns sold candour (Dove r/eal reviews won six Cannes Lions; Burger King retired its mascot; Aerie rejected AI content). Method1's Allison Arling-Giorgi: 'The pratfall effect basically allows you to admit a flaw.'

FTC complaints (allegations, not findings) in Oct 2026 include fabricated positive reviews and suppressing negative reviews (refunds conditioned on non-disparagement, fake BBB pages). Enforcement of the Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule is active.

lenses.verification: Dove numbers are Unilever self-reported (impressions, queues); no sales figure: say so. Spiegel 4.0-4.7 is a 2017 analysis, sample not on page: say 'research' not 'all shoppers'. Pratfall original N=48 men, 1966; key caveat: flaw helps ONLY when competence is clear (average candidate lost liking): this caveat is the story, not a footnote. FTC items are allegations; caption only, no names of alleged schemes on screen.
lenses.audience_psychology: Every owner fears the one-star review and is tempted to hide or delete it; the reveal that perfection reads as fake is counter-intuitive and relieving. Strong save/share: 'send to the person who deletes bad reviews'.
lenses.brand_fit: Brand trust, communication, reviews: core marketing; daily utility for small businesses on Instagram/Google Maps in Persian and international markets. Different from 11-06 (loud vs real reactions) and 11-08 (being fooled by AI): this is about showing your own flaw on purpose.

candidates.story_gate: Tension: you hide the flaw to look trustworthy, the hiding makes you less trustworthy. Image: a spilled coffee cup (the 1966 pratfall) and a 5-star row with one star dimmed.

pick_reason: Highest total and strongest story gate: a counter-intuitive tension (hiding the flaw is what makes you look untrustworthy) with concrete images (the spilled coffee cup of the 1966 pratfall study; a five-star row with one star dimmed; Dove printing a 'smells like expired hotel shampoo' review on its own ad). Universal for Persian and international small-business owners who live on Instagram and map reviews. Evergreen core with 2026 campaign evidence and an Oct-Nov 2026 enforcement spark. No overlap with the last 7 days.
